title: Two pet shops on Shopify POS: how do you handle supplier invoices and repricing
text: Hi! I run two independent pet shops in the UK. We use Shopify POS and Sumtracker, and buy from around 100 suppliers. Two things eat a lot of time: 1. invoices and repricing When stock arrives, we manually check each invoice line against the cost in Shopify. If a price has gone up, we work out the new retail price to hold our margin, update Shopify, tell both shops, and print new shelf labels, It’s v slow/mnaual and price rises slip through. 2. Comparing suppliers Most suppliers want orders through their portals, promotions arrive by email, website or rep, and we have to hit minimum order quantities. In practice, we often just stick with the usual supplier because comparing/optimising takes too long How do you handle these? Any tools or workflows that actually work with lots of suppliers and multiple locations, or is it spreadsheets for everyone? 13 posts - 9 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Retail shop owner spending too much time manually checking supplier invoices and updating prices across locations.

title: Finance Summary report
text: We use the daily Finance Summary report to obtain our sales/Vat figures. The problem we are having concerns the difference between the sales total and the payments by Gateway total. The nature of our business means that customers often pay deposits and can take weeks to pay the balance and complete their orders. Shopify records the order as a sale once any form of partial payment is received. This means that our sales figures are inaccurate. We have huge discrepancies between the total sales and total payments by Gateway. Shopify suggested creating draft orders only but that idea is no use as Shopify converts them to sales as soon as any form of payment is taken. Reconciling these figures has become a nightmare especially as we come to the end of the year. Does anyone have any suggestions or a workaround ? 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant struggling with inaccurate sales totals and year-end financial reconciliation due to partial deposit workflows.

title: How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
text: Curious how other guys handle this. I'll quote a job based on what I can see, then get into a wall or under a floor and find rot, bad wiring, whatever — something there was no way to know about walking through it. Now I've got to have the "this is going to cost more" conversation, and even when I'm straight with people about why, some of them hear it as "the guy padded the price after he had me locked in." Had one a while back where the homeowner got a few other quotes after mine changed... How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
triage_reason: Contractor dealing with the recurring operational pain of mid-job surprise discoveries and client pushback on cost changes.
